component: EC125 Adiabatic Compressed Air Energy Storage (A-CAES)
description: Round-trip efficiency model for A-CAES. Heat of compression stored in thermal energy storage (TES) and returned on discharge — no supplemental fuel. RTE higher than diabatic CAES due to recovered heat.

unit.name: Generic Adiabatic CAES (ADELE-class, 360 MW / 2880 MWh)
unit.source: Barbour, E., et al. (2015). A review on pumped power storage systems. Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews, 45, 598-614; Budt, M. et al. (2016). Applied Energy, 170, 250-268; Wolf, D. & Budt, M. (2014). LTA-CAES: A low-temperature approach to adiabatic CAES. Applied Energy, 125, 158-164.

eta_compressor.note: Polytropic compressor train efficiency (higher than diabatic due to multi-stage with intercooling to TES)

eta_expander.note: Turbine train efficiency (higher than diabatic; pre-heated by TES)

eta_tes.note: Thermal energy storage round-trip efficiency (ratio of heat returned to heat stored); governs A-CAES vs diabatic gap

cavern_volume.note: Same cavern class as Huntorf for comparison

specific_work.note: Compressor specific work per kg air (higher than diabatic; no fuel supplement, more compression stages)

specific_expansion_adiabatic.note: Expander specific energy per kg air using TES-recovered heat; calibrated to RTE~70%: E_out=335*0.86*0.97=279.9 kJ/kg; E_in=310/(0.80*0.97)=399.5 kJ/kg; RTE=279.9/399.5=0.700. Lower than compression work (310 kJ/kg) because TES and duct losses reduce heat returned.

heat_rate.note: No supplemental fuel — adiabatic mode; heat comes from TES only
